memory_bridge: Use two matching mouth-shaped pieces in three steps: their total is written 合計 with On ゴウ; by themselves they come together with 合う, Kun あう; and a person actively aligns them with 合わせる, Kun あわせる.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 合計（ごうけい）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Count the fitted pieces on a receipt labeled 合計（ごうけい）, “sum total”; the first character uses On ゴウ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 合う（あう）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Let the two curved pieces slide together until they 合う（あう）; the complete native verb fixes Kun あう, “to come together.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 合わせる（あわせる）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Now have a musician deliberately align two beats and 合わせる（あわせる） their rhythm; the complete native verb fixes Kun あわせる, “to match.”

memory_bridge: Turn the crescent into a calendar dial: point to 月曜日 for On ゲツ, flip to 一月 for On ガツ, then lift the dial into the night sky and call the moon 月 for Kun つき.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 月曜日（げつようび）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Circle 月曜日（げつようび） beneath the crescent on the weekly dial; its first character sounds On ゲツ in “Monday.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 一月（いちがつ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Flip the same moon dial to 一月（いちがつ）, “January”; the final character now uses the calendar-month On sound ガツ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 月（つき）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Lift the crescent off the calendar and into the sky, naming the celestial body 月（つき）; the standalone native word fixes Kun つき, “Moon.”

memory_bridge: Split simplified 发 into its two traditional identities: 發 emits a discovery flag in 发现 with high-level fā; 髮 is a strand of hair, whose citation reading is falling fà, though 头发 commonly realizes that syllable lightly as tóu fa. The flag and hair strand prevent the merged shape from merging the readings.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 发现 is a common modern anchor for this distinct reading.
readings.overlay: The hand flicks a discovery flag outward as the detective shouts 发现（fā xiàn）, “found it”; hold fā high and level. This sense corresponds to traditional 發.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 头发 is a common modern anchor for this distinct reading.
readings.overlay: A strand of 头发（tóu fa）, “hair,” falls from the head. Remember the dictionary form as falling fà and traditional 髮, while the anchor word’s second syllable is commonly light fa.
